lines: A heart says it. A reply answers one message. This is react and reply.
Press and hold a message, or focus it and press Enter. Message actions opens.
Five quick reactions, More reactions, Reply and Copy.
Pick the heart. A chip shows under the message: the heart, its count, and pressed, because it's yours.
Choose your chip again, and your reaction goes. A chip that reaches zero goes too.
More reactions has twelve more, pancakes among them.
And what the others choose shows as it happens.
If a reaction doesn't save, it goes back, and says so, with Try again.
Copy puts the message on the clipboard.
Reply shows Replying to Ruth, one line of her message, and Cancel reply.
Send, and your reply carries a quote: her first name and one line.
Choose a quote, and the thread goes to that message and marks it for two seconds, loading earlier messages if it must.
On your own message, there is Delete too. It asks first: Delete this message?
A reply to it stays, and its quote reads Message deleted.
In a direct message, it all works the same way, and only the two of you see it.

lines.text: On a phone, Message actions rises from the bottom.
From a tablet up, it opens over the thread.

lines: Once the Popkin wraps up, chips and quotes stay, but nothing can be changed.
What no screen shows: one reaction per member per emoji, held by the API, and a version on each message's reactions, so an older update never wins.
A direct message's reactions reach its two members alone, and no log carries the emoji.
That is journey twelve. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
